Wrap logic in try/catch blocks.\\\\n\\\\n- 200: OK\\\\n- 201: Created\\\\n- 400: Bad Request (Validation Error)\\\\n- 401: Unauthorized (Auth Error)\\\\n- 403: Forbidden (Permission Error)\\\\n- 404: Not Found\\\\n- 500: Internal Server Error\\\\n- Use `'use server'` to define mutations.\\\\n- Validate and coerce inputs on the server; never trust client data.\\\\n- Keep actions small and idempotent where possible.\\\\n- Revalidate as needed after mutations.\\\\n- Prefer static metadata where possible for performance.\\\\n- Use `generateMetadata` for dynamic routes; avoid heavy computations.\\\\n- Provide titles, descriptions, and canonical URLs.\\\\n- Select appropriate fetch cache mode per route: `force-cache`, `no-store`, or revalidation interval.\\\\n- Use segment-level `dynamic` or `revalidate` where needed.\\\\n- Avoid over-caching user-specific content.\\\\n- Keep middleware **small** and **edge-compatible**.\\\\n- Scope aggressively with `config.matcher`; avoid running on `_next` assets.\\\\n- Avoid project-specific routes; use placeholders.\\\\n\\\\n### Minimal illustrative pattern\\\\n\\\\n```ts\\\\nimport { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server'\\\\n\\\\nexport function middleware(request: NextRequest) {\\\\n  const token = request.cookies.get('auth_token')\\\\n  const isProtected = request.nextUrl.pathname.startsWith('<protected-prefix>')\\\\n\\\\n  if (isProtected && !token) {\\\\n    return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/login', request.url))\\\\n  }\\\\n\\\\n  return NextResponse.next()\\\\n}\\\\n\\\\nexport const config = {\\\\n  matcher: ['/((?!api|_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico).*)'],\\\\n}\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n### Concrete Checks\\\\n- Use the App Router (`app/` directory) and Server Components by default.\\\\n- API endpoints implemented as `route.ts` handlers under `app/api/...`.\\\\n- Mutations use Server Actions with proper input validation on the server.\\\\n- Metadata configured via `generateMetadata` or static export where appropriate.\\\\n- Apply appropriate caching strategy (`dynamic`, `revalidate`) per route.\\\\n\\\\n## Tailwind CSS Validation Context\\\\n\\\\n### Guidelines\\\\n❌ Wrong (v3):\\\\n```\\\\n@tailwind base;\\\\n@tailwind components;\\\\n@tailwind utilities;\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n✅ Correct (v4):\\\\n```\\\\n@import \\\\\\\"tailwindcss\\\\\\\";\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n- Avoid legacy `@apply` usage in component files; Add `font-sans` on the root layout and any text elements to avoid Times New Roman fallbacks.\\\\n\\\\n## Rule 3 — Prefer arbitrary values for custom palette\\\\n\\\\nWhen you need colors outside the design tokens, use arbitrary values (e.g., `bg-[#0a0a0a]`, `text-[#e8e8e8]`). Avoid guessing with the default Tailwind palette when a precise value is required.\\\\n\\\\n## Rule 4 — Clear build cache after CSS changes\\\\n\\\\nIf utilities stop applying, clear the framework cache before debugging:\\\\n\\\\n```bash\\\\nrm -rf .next && npm run dev\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nStale `.next` artifacts are a common source of \\\\\\\"class not found\\\\\\\" issues in v4.\\\\n\\\\n## Rule 5 — Use the v4 PostCSS preset\\\\n\\\\nConfigure PostCSS with the official v4 preset and avoid the legacy plugin:\\\\n\\\\n```js\\\\n// postcss.config.mjs\\\\nexport default {\\\\n  plugins: {\\\\n    '@tailwindcss/postcss': {}, // ✅ v4 preset\\\\n  },\\\\n}\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nThe legacy `tailwindcss` plugin will fail to generate utilities in v4.\\\\n\\\\n## Rule 6 — Define tokens in `@theme`\\\\n\\\\nExpress design tokens as CSS variables inside an `@theme` block so components stay in sync wies\\\\n### TDD workflow (Vitest)\\\\n\\\\n- Follow core TDD (see constitution): tests-first, minimal green, then refactor.\\\\n- Keep the loop tight: run the smallest scope that proves correctness, then expand.\\\\n\\\\n#### Micro-template\\\\n\\\\n```typescript\\\\nimport { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest'\\\\n\\\\ndescribe('feature', () => {\\\\n  it('RED: fails before implementation exists', () => {\\\\n    // Arrange\\\\n    // Act\\\\n    // Assert\\\\n    expect(actual).toEqual(expected)\\\\n  })\\\\n})\\\\n```\\\\n### Test quality (Vitest)\\\\n\\\\n- Use descriptive `describe`/`it` names that state **behavior**.\\\\n- Prefer outcome assertions over internal call assertions.\\\\n- Prefer user-facing assertions for UI; `loading.tsx` and `error.tsx`.\\\\n- In Next.js 16 App Router, prefer Server Components by default; mark Client Components with `'use client'` only when strictly necessary.\\\\nRoute Handlers allow you to create custom request handlers for a given route using the Web Request and Response APIs.\\\\n\\\\n## Convention\\\\n\\\\n- Implement handlers in `app/api/<versiononse.json({ error: 'Unauthorized' }, { status: 401 });\\\\n  }\\\\n  \\\\n  return NextResponse.json({ data: 'Protected data' });\\\\n}\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n## Input Validation with Zod\\\\n\\\\nAlways validate incoming data structure and types using Zod.\\\\n\\\\n```typescript\\\\nimport { z } from 'zod';\\\\nimport { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';\\\\n\\\\nconst schema = z.object({\\\\n  id: z.string().uuid(),\\\\n  quantity: z.number().int().positive(),\\\\n});\\\\n\\\\nexport async function POST(request: NextRequest) {\\\\n  try {\\\\n    const body = await request.json();\\\\n    const data = schema.parse(body);\\\\n    // Process valid data...\\\\n    return NextResponse.json({ success: true });\\\\n  } catch (error) {\\\\n     return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Invalid input' }, { status: 400 });\\\\n  }\\\\n}\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n## Dynamic Route Parameters\\\\n\\\\nRoute handlers can access dynamic segment parameters.\\\\n\\\\nFile: `app/api/items/[id]/route.ts`\\\\n\\\\n```typescript\\\\nimport { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';\\\\n\\\\nexport async function GET(\\\\n  request: NextRequest,\\\\n  { params }: { params: { id: string } }\\\\n) {\\\\n  const id = params.id; // Access dynamic param\\\\n  return NextResponse.json({ id });\\\\n}\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n## Error Handling\\\\n\\\\nUse standard HTTP status codes and consistent error response formats. Wrap logic in try/catch blocks.\\\\n\\\\n- 200: OK\\\\n- 201: Created\\\\n- 400: Bad Request (Validation Error)\\\\n- 401: Unauthorized (Auth Error)\\\\n- 403: Forbidden (Permission Error)\\\\n- 404: Not Found\\\\n- 500: Internal Server Error\\\\n- Use `'use server'` to define mutations.\\\\n- Validate and coerce inputs on the server; never trust client data.\\\\n- Keep actions small and idempotent where possible.\\\\n- Revalidate as needed after mutations.\\\\n- Prefer static metadata where possible for performance.\\\\n- Use `generateMetadata` for dynamic routes; avoid heavy computations.\\\\n- Provide titles, descriptions, and canonical URLs.\\\\n- Select appropriate fetch cache mode per route: `force-cache`, `no-store`, or revalidation interval.\\\\n- Use segment-erver Actions with proper input validation on the server.\\\\n- Metadata configured via `generateMetadata` or static export where appropriate.\\\\n- Apply appropriate caching strategy (`dynamic`, `revalidate`) per route.\\\\n\\\\n## Tailwind CSS Validation Context\\\\n\\\\n### Guidelines\\\\n❌ Wrong (v3):\\\\n```\\\\n@tailwind base;\\\\n@tailwind components;\\\\n@tailwind utilities;\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n✅ Correct (v4):\\\\n```\\\\n@import \\\\\\\"tailwindcss\\\\\\\";\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n- Avoid legacy `@apply` usage in component files; prefer design tokens, utility classes, or `@layer` definitions instead.\\\\n\\\\n## Rule 1 — Import syntax only\\\\n\\\\nUse the v4 CSS-first import at the top of the global stylesheet:\\\\n\\\\n```css\\\\n@import \\\\\\\"tailwindcss\\\\\\\";\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nDo **not** use v3 directives (`@tailwind base|components|utilities`) because they are ignored by v4.\\\\n\\\\n## Rule 2 — Apply `font-sans` explicitly\\\\n\\\\nTailwind v4 no longer injects the default font stack automatically. Add `font-sans` on the root layout and any text elements to avoid Times Newsync with the theme source of truth:\\\\n\\\\n```css\\\\n@theme {\\\\n  --color-surface: oklch(18% 0.02 260);\\\\n  --color-border: oklch(28% 0.03 260);\\\\n  --font-sans: \\\\\\\"Inter\\\\\\\", system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif;\\\\n}\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nUse the generated classes (`bg-surface`, `border-border`, `font-sans`) instead of hardcoding values in components.\\\\n\\\\n- Centralize color, spacing, and typography via CSS variables when feasible.\\\\n- Prefer utilities referencing tokens; avoid ad-hoc hardcoded values.\\\\n- Document tokens and usage for contributors.\\\\n- Use mobile-first styles; apply breakpoints progressively.\\\\n- Prefer container queries where available; avoid fragile CSS overrides.\\\\n- Test across common device sizes and high-contrast modes.\\\\n\\\\n### Concrete Checks\\\\n- Use Tailwind v4 import syntax (no `@tailwind base/components/utilities`).\\\\n- Apply `font-sans` to text elements by default.\\\\n- Prefer utility classes; minimize custom CSS.\\\\n- Support light and dark modes.\\\\n\\\\n## Vitest Validation Context\\\\n\\\\n### Guidelines\\\\n### TDD workflow (Vitest)\\\\n\\\\n- Follow core TDD (see constitution): tests-first, minimal green, then refactor.\\\\n- Keep the loop tight: run the smallest scope that proves correctness, then expand.\\\\n\\\\n#### Micro-template\\\\n\\\\n```typescript\\\\nimport { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest'\\\\n\\\\ndescribe('feature', () => {\\\\n  it('RED: fails before implementation exists', () => {\\\\n    // Arrange\\\\n    // Act\\\\n    // Assert\\\\n    expect(actual).toEqual(expected)\\\\n  })\\\\n})\\\\n```\\\\n### Test quality (Vitest)\\\\n\\\\n- Use descriptive `describe`/`it` names that state **behavior**.\\\\n- Prefer outcome assertions over internal call assertions.\\\\n- Prefer user-facing assertions for UI; avoid brittle snapshots unless they add real value.\\\\n- Ensure proper setup/teardown; avoid shared mutable state.\\\\n\\\\n#### GOOD: behavior-focused, outcome assertions\\\\n\\\\n```typescript\\\\nimport { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest'\\\\n\\\\ndescribe('createItem', () => {\\\\n  it('rejects empty name with a typed error', () => {\\\\n    expect(() => createItem({ name: '' })).toThrow(/name/i)\\\\n  })\\\\n})\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n#### BAD: implementation-detail assertions as “proof”\\\\n\\\\n```typescript\\\\nimport { it, expect } from 'vitest'\\\\n\\\\nit('creates item', async () => {\\\\n  await createItem({ name: 'x' })\\\\n\\\\n  // ❌ proves only that an internal method was called, not that behavior is correct\\\\n  expect(internalDbClient.insert).toHaveBeenCalled()\\\\n})\\\\n```\\\\n### API testing (Vitest)\\\\n\\\\n- **Test the boundary**: Prefer exercising the real API boundary (real request/response) over calling internal helpers directly.\\\\n- **Assert contracts**: Status codes + response envelope shape + key fields.\\\\n- **Deterministic data**: Use per-test unique IDs / namespaces or transaction rollback (whatever your stack supports) to avoid cross-test collisions.\\\\n- **No internal mocking**: Do not mock internal auth/data/business modules as “proof”. If a boundary double is unavoidable, limit it to **external services you do not control**.\\\\n\\\\n#### Minimal erEvent.setup()\\\\n  render(<MyForm />)\\\\n\\\\n  await user.type(screen.getByLabelText(/email/i), 'a@b.com')\\\\n  await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: /submit/i }))\\\\n\\\\n  expect(await screen.findByText(/success/i)).toBeInTheDocument()\\\\n})\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n### Concrete Checks\\\\n- Avoid `.skip()`/`.only()` in committed code.\\\\n- Enforce the core NO MOCKS policy: mock only system boundaries (third-party APIs), never internal modules.\\\\n- Keep tests fast and deterministic with clear naming.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Output Format\\\\n\\\\n```markdown\\\\n# Global Validation Report\\\\n\\\\n**Task**: [Task ID]\\\\n**Status**: ✅ APPROVED | ⚠️ APPROVED WITH WARNINGS | ❌ REJECTED\\\\n**Timestamp**: [ISO 8601]\\\\n\\\\n## Summary\\\\n[2-3 sentences]\\\\n\\\\n## Validation Results\\\\n### 1-10. Everything internal must be real.\\\\n\\\\n## Quality Principles (All Roles)\\\\n\\\\n### Type Safety\\\\n- No untyped escape hatches\\\\n- Justify any type suppressions (language-specific ignore directives, dynamic-typing escape hatches)\\\\n- Type safety settings come from project configuration\\\\n\\\\n### Code Hygiene\\\\n- No TODO/FIXME placeholders in production code\\\\n- No stray console.log or debug statements\\\\n- Remove dead code\\\\n- No commented-out code blocks\\\\n\\\\n### Error Handling\\\\n- Async flows expose clear `loading` / `error` / `empty` states\\\\n- Errors are properly caught and handled\\\\n- User-facing errors are meaningful\\\\n\\\\n### DRY & SOLID\\\\n- No code duplication—extract to shared utilities\\\\n- Single Responsibility Principle\\\\n- Open/Closed Principle\\\\n- Liskov Substitution Principle\\\\n- Interface Segregation Principle\\\\n- Dependency Inversion Principle\\\\n\\\\n### Configuration-First\\\\n- No hardcoded values—all config from YAML\\\\n- No magic numbers or strings in code\\\\n- Every behavior must be configurable\\\\n\\\\n## Configuration-First Principles (All Roles)\\\\n\\\\n### Core Rule\\\\nNO hardcoded values. ALL configuration comes from YAML.\\\\n\\\\n### What Must Be Configurable\\\\n- Feature flags\\\\n- Thresholds and limits\\\\n- Timeouts and intervals\\\\n- API endpoints\\\\n- Credentials (via environment)\\\\n- Behavior toggles\\\\n\\\\n### Benefits\\\\n- Change behavior without code changes\\\\n- Environment-specific settings\\\\n- Audit trail for configuration\\\\n- Easier testing (override config)\\\\n\\\\n### Config Hierarchy\\\\n```\\\\nDefault (code) → Core YAML → Pack YAML → Project YAML → Environment\\\\n```\\\\nLater layers override earlier ones.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Git Safety (Non-Negotiable)\\\\n- **Never switch branches in the primary checkout.** Edison/LLMs MUST NOT run `git checkout` / `git switch` in the primary worktree.\\\\n- **Branch creation/deletion is restricted.** Only create/delete branches via Edison session/worktree commands unless the user explicitly asks otherwise.\\\\n- **NEVER use `git reset`, `git restore`, `git clean`, `git checkout -- <file>`, or any other destructive commands without user approval.** If you see unrelated changes/work to what you expect, NEVER discard them without explicit user confirmation. Many agents/LLMs may be working on the same task concurrently, so \\\\\\\"unrelated\\\\\\\" changes is expected and you should NEVER discard them, except via explicit user instruction.\\\\n\\\\n- Do **not** create ad-hoc summary/report/status files.\\\\n- Task + QA files under `.project/tasks/` and `.project/qa/` are the only approved tracking artifacts.\\\\n- Track progress in tasks/QA and git history (do not create parallel documents):\\\\n  - Task directories (`todo`, `wip`, `blocked`, `done`, `validated`) – implementation status + delegation logs.\\\\n  - QA directories (`waiting`, `todo`, `wip`, `done`, `validated`) – validator assignments, findings, verdicts, evidence links.\\\\n    - `.project/qa/waiting/` = QA created, waiting for task to reach `done/`\\\\n    - `.project/qa/todo/` = Ready to validate NOW (task is in `done/`)\\\\n  - Git history – commits tied to task IDs (mention ID in commit body when useful).\\\\n- Validation artefacts belong under `.project/qa/validation-evidence/<task-id>/round-<N>/` and must be referenced from the QA document.\\\\n- Archive/analysis files go under `docs/archive/` only when explicitly requested.\\\\n- Before marking work complete, ensure there are no stray `*_SUMMARY.md` / `*_ANALYSIS.md` files or similar; delete unapproved summaries and rely on the canonical directories.\\\\n\\\\n## principles\\\\n\\\\nDefault to human-readable CLI output.\\\\n\\\\n- Prefer plain text/Markdown output when reading command results inside an LLM conversation.\\\\n- Use `--json` only when you need structured output for tools/scripts or when explicitly requested.\\\\n\\\\n## validator\\\\n\\\\nValidators should default to non-JSON output while reviewing. Use `--json` only when it is explicitly needed for structured extraction or reporting.\\\\n\\\\n## principles\\\\n\\\\nRun shell commands via Edison whenever possible:\\\\n\\\\n- Prefer `edison exec -- <command> [args...]` for command execution.\\\\n- This enables safety shims (when configured) and records audit events for executed commands.\\\\n- If you have a persistent shell, you may additionally enable shims once:\\\\n  - `edison shims sync`\\\\n  - `eval \\\\\\\"$(edison shims env)\\\\\\\"`\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## TDD Compliance Checking (Validators)\\\\n\\\\n### Verification Checklist\\\\n- [ ] Tests exist in appropriate test directory\\\\n- [ ] Test file created BEFORE implementation (check git history)\\\\n- [ ] Tests cover the requirements specified in task\\\\n\\\\n### Red Phase Evidence\\\\n- [ ] Sub-agent showed tests failing initially\\\\n- [ ] Failure messages indicate tests were actually testing something\\\\n- [ ] No skipped/disabled tests or commented-out tests\\\\n\\\\n### Green Phase Evidence\\\\n- [ ] All tests now passing\\\\n- [ ] No tests were removed or weakened to pass\\\\n- [ ] Coverage meets minimum threshold\\\\n\\\\n### Refactor Phase (if applicable)\\\\n- [ ] Tests still pass after refactoring\\\\n- [ ] Code is cleaner without changing behavior\\\\n- [ ] No new functionality added during refactor\\\\n\\\\n### Red Flags (Immediate Rejection)\\\\n🚩 **Immediate Rejection:**\\\\n- Tests written AFTER implementation (check git history)\\\\n- Tests that always pass (no assertions)\\\\n- Mocked everything (no real behavior tested)\\\\n- Test-only production methods/flags added solely to enable tests\\\\n- Tests primarily assert on call counts/spies instead of observable behavior\\\\n- Coverage below threshold with no justification\\\\n- Tests removed to make suite pass\\\\n\\\\n🟡 **Needs Review:**\\\\n- Coverage just barely meets threshold\\\\n- Complex tests that are hard to understand\\\\n- Tests coupled to implementation details\\\\n- Missing edge case coverage\\\\n- Boundary mocks/fixtures that appear incomplete or drift from real schemas\\\\n\\\\n## NO MOCKS Validation (Validators)\\\\n\\\\n### Patterns to Flag (Blocking)\\\\n\\\\nFlag any use of mocking/stubbing/spying facilities applied to **internal code** (data access, authentication, business logic, domain services).\\\\n\\\\nExamples of what to flag (language-agnostic):\\\\n- Importing a mocking library and substituting internal modules/classes/functions\\\\n- Stubbing/spying on internal service methods as “proof” instead of asserting outcomes\\\\n- Replacing the real database/data-layer client with a fake object\\\\n- Replacing real authentication/authorization with fakes\\\\n\\\\n### Immediate Rejection Triggers\\\\n🚩 **Reject if found:**\\\\n- Database client mocked\\\\n- Authentication flows mocked\\\\n- Internal service modules mocked\\\\n- Using `toHaveBeenCalled` on internal methods as proof\\\\n\\\\n### Acceptable Exceptions\\\\n✅ **May allow:**\\\\n- External API mocks (payment gateways, email services)\\\\n- Third-party service mocks at boundaries\\\\n- Clock/timer mocks for time-sensitive tests\\\\n\\\\n### Validation Questions\\\\n1. Does this test exercise real code paths?\\\\n2. Would this test catch a real production bug?\\\\n3. Is the mock at a true system boundary?\\\\n\\\\n## Quality Validation (Validators)\\\\n\\\\n### Type Safety Check\\\\n- [ ] No type-system escape hatches without justification\\\\n- [ ] No ignore directives without an explicit rationale\\\\n- [ ] Project type-safety settings are enforced\\\\n\\\\n### Code Smell Check\\\\n- [ ] No god classes (excessive responsibilities)\\\\n- [ ] No feature envy (manipulating other class's data)\\\\n- [ ] No inappropriate intimacy (reaching into internals)\\\\n- [ ] Functions under 30 lines\\\\n- [ ] No deep nesting (max 3 levels)\\\\n- [ ] No hidden side effects\\\\n\\\\n### Naming Check\\\\n- [ ] Names are clear about purpose\\\\n- [ ] No abbreviations without context\\\\n- [ ] Consistent naming across modules\\\\n- [ ] Boolean names are positive\\\\n\\\\n### Duplication Check\\\\n- [ ] No copy-pasted logic\\\\n- [ ] No reimplemented standard library functions\\\\n- [ ] Repeated validation centralized\\\\n- [ ] Single source of truth for constants\\\\n\\\\n### Architecture Check\\\\n- [ ] No tight coupling between modules\\\\n- [ ] No circular dependencies\\\\n- [ ] No global mutable state\\\\n- [ ] No layer violations\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Context7 Knowledge Refresh (CRITICAL)\\\\n\\\\nUse Context7 to refresh your knowledge **before** implementing or validating when work touches any configured post-training package.\\\\n\\\\n- Project overrides live in `.edison/config/context7.yaml`.\\\\n- To view the merged effective Context7 configuration (core → packs → user → project), run: `edison Within Session Scope\\\\nBefore expanding scope, prioritize validation work already inside the current session:\\\\n- Validate owned/paired QA briefs tied to tasks you already own before claiming new RULE.GIT.NO_DESTRUCTIVE_DEFAULT: Never “clean up” unrelated diffs with destructive git\\\\nNever revert, reset, or “clean up” unrelated/uncommitted changes unless the user explicitly asks.\\\\n\\\\nIn multi-LLM sessions it is normal to see unrelated diffs from other in-flight work. Do not:\\\\n- run `git reset`, `git restore`, `git clean`, `git checkout -- <path>`, `git switch`, etc.\\\\n- delete or revert “unwanted modifications” on your own initiative\\\\n\\\\nIf you believe a change is truly accidental, escalate and ask before taking any destructive action.\\\\n\\\\nReference: `guidelines/shared/GIT_WORKFLOW.md`\\\\n\\\\n### RULE.VALIDATION.INDEPENDENCE: Orchestrator Cannot Self-Validate\\\\nValidation must be independent:\\\\n- Orchestrator must not validate their own implementation work.\\\\n- Use separate validator roles/models where possible; otherwise create the task without linking.\\\\n\\\\nReference: `guidelines/orchestrators/SESSION_WORKFLOW.md`\\\\n\\\\n### RULE.FOLLOWUPS.DEDUPE_FIRST: Deduplicate follow-ups before creating tasks\\\\nBefore creating follow-ups:\\\\n- Search for existing tasks/QA covering the same issue.\\\\n- Prefer linking/reusing an existing follow-up over creating duplicates.\\\\n\\\\nReference: `guidelines/orchestrators/SESSION_WORKFLOW.md`\\\\n\\\\n### RULE.FOLLOWUPS.CREATE_NO_LINK_FOR_SOFT: Create non-blocking validator follow-ups without linking\\\\nNon-blocking follow-ups must not gate promotion:\\\\n- Create the follow-up task so it’s tracked.\\\\n- Do NOT link it as a child unless it is explicitly blocking.\\\\n\\\\nReference: `guidelines/shared/VALIDATION.md`\\\\n\\\\n### RULE.CONTEXT.BUDGET_MINIMIZE: Preserve context budget – load only what's needed\\\\nPreserve context budget:\\\\n- Load only the minimum files/sections necessary for the current decision.\\\\n- Prefer diffs + focused snippets over whole files.\\\\n\\\\nReference: `guidelines/orchestrators/SESSION_WORKFLOW.md`\\\\n\\\\n### RULE.CONTEXT.NO_BIG_FILES: Do not load big files unless necessary\\\\nAvoid loading huge inputs:\\\\n- Do not paste logs/build artefacts/large generated files into prompts.\\\\n- Extract only the minimal relevant excerpt and reference the full artifact by path.\\\\n\\\\nReference: `guidelines/orchestrators/SESSION_WORKFLOW.md`\\\\n\\\\n### RULE.CONTEXT.SNIPPET_ONLY: Share snippets not whole files in prompts\\\\nShare snippets, not entire files:\\\\n- Provide the minimal relevant function/component/section with small surrounding context.\\\\n- Combine multiple small snippets when cross-references are required instead of dumping a full file.\\\\n\\\\nReference: `guidelines/orchestrators/SESSION_WORKFLOW.md`\\\\n\\\\n### RULE.NEXTJS.APP_ROUTER: Use App Router\\\\nAll routes must use App Router (app/ directory), not Pages Router. You ONLY see:\\\\n1. The task requirements\\\\n2. The git diff\\\\n3. The current codebase state\\\\n\\\\nYour validation must be **thorough, objective, and unbiased**.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Review Philosophy\\\\n\\\\n**Channel the exacting standards of Linus Torvalds** (without the profanity).\\\\n\\\\n- 🔍 **Thorough**: Don't skip edge cases, error paths, or security implications\\\\n- 🎯 **Direct**: Call out issues clearly and specifically\\\\n- 📏 **Exacting**: Production quality means PRODUCTION quality\\\\n- 🚫 **No \\\\\\\"Good Enough\\\\\\\"**: \\\\\\\"Works on my machine\\\\\\\" is not acceptable\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Validation Workflow\\\\n\\\\n### Step 1: Context7 Knowledge Refresh\\\\nRefresh your knowledge on post-training packages used in this project BEFORE validating.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 2: Review Git Diff\\\\n\\\\n```bash\\\\ngit diff --cached  # Staged changes\\\\ngit diff           # Unstaged changes\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n**Questions to Answer**:\\\\n1. ✅ **Scope Compliance**: Do changes satisfy the task requirements?\\\\n2. ✅ **Unintended Deletions**: Was any code accidentally removed?\\\\n3. ✅ **Regression Risk**: Could changes break existing functionality?\\\\n4. ✅ **Security Vulnerabilities**: Do changes introduce security holes?\\\\n5. ✅ **Performance Impact**: Do changes affect performance?\\\\n6. ✅ **Dependency Risk**: If `package.json` / lockfiles changed, did any vulnerable package **versions** change due to this task?\\\\n\\\\n**Scope Guidance (Important):**\\\\n- Treat \\\\\\\"extra/unrelated diffs\\\\\\\" as a **warning**, not an automatic rejection.\\\\n- Only **reject for scope drift** when the extra changes are clearly risky/unintentional (e.g., broad refactors, unrelated dependency/config churn, suspicious deletions, security-sensitive changes) or when they directly violate the task constraints.\\\\n- Your goal is to prevent defects, not to punish multi-agent workflows where other work may exist in the checkout.\\\\n\\\\n**Dependency audit policy (change-aware):**\\\\n- If `package.json` / lockfiles changed, assess dependency risk for the **delta introduced by this task**.\\\\n- If lockfiles changed but vulnerable package **versions** did **not** change (normalization/reordering), do **not** reject solely on baseline audit findings; create follow-up tasks instead.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 3: Run 10-Point Comprehensive Checklist\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 10-Point Checklist\\\\n\\\\n### 1. `\\\\\\\"strict\\\\\\\": true`.\\\\n- Prefer `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `noImplicitOverride`, `noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature`.\\\\n\\\\n```json\\\\n{\\\\n  \\\\\\\"compilerOptions\\\\\\\": {\\\\n    \\\\\\\"strict\\\\\\\": true,\\\\n    \\\\\\\"noUncheckedIndexedAccess\\\\\\\": true\\\\n  }\\\\n}\\\\n```\\\\n- Prefer discriminated unions over optional fields.\\\\n- Use `satisfies` for config objects (prevents excess properties without widening).\\\\n- Constrain generics.\\\\n\\\\n```ts\\\\ntype Result =\\\\n  | { ok: true; value: string }\\\\n  | { ok: false; error: string }\\\\n\\\\nconst cfg = {\\\\n  mode: 'prod',\\\\n} satisfies { mode: 'prod' | 'dev' }\\\\n```\\\\n- Prefer `as const` for literal inference; avoid overusing `as` assertions.\\\\n- Use template literal types for expressive keys.\\\\n\\\\n```ts\\\\ntype EventName = `user.${'created' | 'deleted'}`\\\\n\\\\nconst status = {\\\\n  active: 'active',\\\\n  archived: 'archived',\\\\n} as const\\\\n\\\\ntype Status = (typeof status)[keyof typeof status]\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n### Type Safety\\\\n- Enforce `strict` mode for all TS projects.\\\\n- Avoid `any` unless justified with comments and tests.\\\\n- Prefer explicit return types on exported functions.\\\\n- For public APIs, use interfaces/types with clear generics.\\\\n\\\\n### Linting & Type-Checking\\\\n- `{{fn:ci_command(\\\\\\\"type-check\\\\\\\")}}` must pass with zero errors.\\\\n- No `@ts-ignore` or `@ts-expect-error` without issue link and scope.\\\\n\\\\n## Next.js Validation Context\\\\n\\\\n### Guidelines\\\\n- Organize routes under `app/` using nested folders, `page.tsx`, and `layout.tsx`.\\\\n- Co-locate loading and error UI with `loading.tsx` and `error.tsx`.\\\\n- In Next.js 16 App Router, prefer Server Components by default; mark Client Components with `'use client'` only when strictly necessary.\\\\nRoute Handlers allow you to create custom request handlers for a given route using the Web Request and Response APIs.\\\\n\\\\n## Convention\\\\n\\\\n- Implement handlers in `app/api/<version>/<resource>/route.ts`.\\\\n- Keep handler thin; delegate business logic to modules.\\\\n- Use `NextRequest` and `NextResponse` from `next/server`.\\\\n\\\\n## HTTP Methods\\\\n\\\\nSupport for standard HTTP methods: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `HEAD`, and `OPTIONS`.\\\\n\\\\n### Example: GET and POST\\\\n\\\\n```typescript\\\\nimport { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';\\\\nimport { z } from 'zod';\\\\n\\\\nexport async function GET(request: NextRequest) {\\\\n  // Handle GET request\\\\n  return NextResponse.json({ message: 'Hello from GET' });\\\\n}\\\\n\\\\nconst createSchema = z.object({\\\\n  title: z.string().min(1),\\\\n});\\\\n\\\\nexport async function POST(request: NextRequest) {\\\\n  try {\\\\n    const body = await request.json();\\\\n    const { title } = createSchema.parse(body);\\\\n    \\\\n    // Perform action...\\\\n    \\\\n    return NextResponse.json({ title }, { status: 201 });\\\\n  } catch (error) {\\\\n    if (error instanceof z.ZodError) {\\\\n      return NextResponse.json({ errors: error.errors }, { status: 400 });\\\\n    }\\\\n    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Internal Server Error' }, { status: 500 });\\\\n  }\\\\n}\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n### Example: PUT, PATCH, DELETE\\\\n\\\\n```typescript\\\\nimport { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';\\\\n\\\\nexport async function PUT(request: NextRequest) {\\\\n  return NextResponse.json({ message: 'Updated via PUT' });\\\\n}\\\\n\\\\nexport async function PATCH(request: NextRequest) {\\\\n  return NextResponse.json({ message: 'Partially updated via PATCH' });\\\\n}\\\\n\\\\nexport async function DELETE(request: NextRequest) {\\\\n  return NextResponse.json({ message: 'Deleted' }, { status: 204 });\\\\n}\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n## Authentication Patterns\\\\n\\\\nUse your authentication library (e.g., NextAuth/Auth.js, Clerk, Supabase) to verify sessions.\\\\n\\\\n```typescript\\\\nimport { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';\\\\nimport { auth } from '<auth-module>'; // Example auth import\\\\n\\\\nexport async function GET(request: NextRequest) {\\\\n  const session = await auth();\\\\n  \\\\n  if (!session) {\\\\n    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Unauthorized' }, { status: 401 });\\\\n  }\\\\n  \\\\n  return NextResponse.json({ data: 'Protected data' });\\\\n}\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n## Input Validation with Zod\\\\n\\\\nAlways validate incoming data structure and types using Zod.\\\\n\\\\n```typescript\\\\nimport { z } from 'zod';\\\\nimport { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';\\\\n\\\\nconst schema = z.object({\\\\n  id: z.string().uuid(),\\\\n  quantity: z.number().int().positive(),\\\\n});\\\\n\\\\nexport async function POST(request: NextRequest) {\\\\n  try {\\\\n    const body = await request.json();\\\\n    const data = schema.parse(body);\\\\n    // Process valid data...\\\\n    return NextResponse.json({ success: true });\\\\n  } catch (error) {\\\\n     return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Invalid input' }, { status: 400 });\\\\n  }\\\\n}\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n## Dynamic Route Parameters\\\\n\\\\nRoute handlers can access dynamic segment parameters.\\\\n\\\\nFile: `app/api/items/[id]/route.ts`\\\\n\\\\n```typescript\\\\nimport { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';\\\\n\\\\nexport async function GET(\\\\n  request: NextRequest,\\\\n  { params }: { params: { id: string } }\\\\n) {\\\\n  const id = params.id; // Access dynamic param\\\\n  return NextResponse.json({ id });\\\\n}\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n## Error Handling\\\\n\\\\nUse standard HTTP status codes and consistent error response formats. Wrap logic in try/catch blocks.\\\\n\\\\n- 200: OK\\\\n- 201: Created\\\\n- 400: Bad Request (Validation Error)\\\\n- 401: Unauthorized (Auth Error)\\\\n- 403: Forbidden (Permission Error)\\\\n- 404: Not Found\\\\n- 500: Internal Server Error\\\\n- Use `'use server'` to define mutations.\\\\n- Validate and coerce inputs on the server; never trust client data.\\\\n- Keep actions small and idempotent where possible.\\\\n- Revalidate as needed after mutations.\\\\n- Prefer static metadata where possible for performance.\\\\n- Use `generateMetadata` for dynamic routes; avoid heavy computations.\\\\n- Provide titles, descriptions, and canonical URLs.\\\\n- Select appropriate fetch cache mode per route: `force-cache`, `no-store`, or revalidation interval.\\\\n- Use segment-level `dynamic` or `revalidate` where needed.\\\\n- Avoid over-caching user-specific content.\\\\n- Keep middleware **small** and **edge-compatible**.\\\\n- Scope aggressively with `config.matcher`; avoid running on `_next` assets.\\\\n- Avoid project-specific routes; use placeholders.\\\\n\\\\n### Minimal illustrative pattern\\\\n\\\\n```ts\\\\nimport { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server'\\\\n\\\\nexport function middleware(request: NextRequest) {\\\\n  const token = request.cookies.get('auth_token')\\\\n  const isProtected = request.nextUrl.pathname.startsWith('<protected-prefix>')\\\\n\\\\n  if (isProtected && !token) {\\\\n    return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/login', request.url))\\\\n  }\\\\n\\\\n  return NextResponse.next()\\\\n}\\\\n\\\\nexport const config = {\\\\n  matcher: ['/((?!api|_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico).*)'],\\\\n}\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n### Concrete Checks\\\\n- Use the App Router (`app/` directory) and Server Components by default.\\\\n- API endpoints implemented as `route.ts` handlers under `app/api/...`.\\\\n- Mutations use Server Actions with proper input validation on the server.\\\\n- Metadata configured via `generateMetadata` or static export where appropriate.\\\\n- Apply appropriate caching strategy (`dynamic`, `revalidate`) per route.\\\\n\\\\n## Tailwind CSS Validation Context\\\\n\\\\n### Guidelines\\\\n❌ Wrong (v3):\\\\n```\\\\n@tailwind base;\\\\n@tailwind components;\\\\n@tailwind utilities;\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n✅ Correct (v4):\\\\n```\\\\n@import \\\\\\\"tailwindcss\\\\\\\";\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n- Avoid legacy `@apply` usage in component files; prefer design tokens, utility classes, or `@layer` definitions instead.\\\\n\\\\n## Rule 1 — Import syntax only\\\\n\\\\nUse the v4 CSS-first import at the top of the global stylesheet:\\\\n\\\\n```css\\\\n@import \\\\\\\"tailwindcss\\\\\\\";\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nDo **not** use v3 directives (`@tailwind base|components|utilities`) because they are ignored by v4.\\\\n\\\\n## Rule 2 — Apply `font-sans` explicitly\\\\n\\\\nTailwind v4 no longer injects the default font stack automatically. Add `font-sans` on the root layout and any text elements to avoid Times New Roman fallbacks.\\\\n\\\\n## Rule 3 — Prefer arbitrary values for custom palette\\\\n\\\\nWhen you need colors outside the design tokens, use arbitrary values (e.g., `bg-[#0a0a0a]`, `text-[#e8e8e8]`). Avoid guessing with the default Tailwind palette when a precise value is required.\\\\n\\\\n## Rule 4 — Clear build cache after CSS changes\\\\n\\\\nIf utilities stop applying, clear the framework cache before debugging:\\\\n\\\\n```bash\\\\nrm -rf .next && npm run dev\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nStale `.next` artifacts are a common source of \\\\\\\"class not found\\\\\\\" issues in v4.\\\\n\\\\n## Rule 5 — Use the v4 PostCSS preset\\\\n\\\\nConfigure PostCSS with the official v4 preset and avoid the legacy plugin:\\\\n\\\\n```js\\\\n// postcss.config.mjs\\\\nexport default {\\\\n  plugins: {\\\\n    '@tailwindcss/postcss': {}, // ✅ v4 preset\\\\n  },\\\\n}\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nThe legacy `tailwindcss` plugin will fail to generate utilities in v4.\\\\n\\\\n## Rule 6 — Define tokens in `@theme`\\\\n\\\\nExpress design tokens as CSS variables inside an `@theme` block so components stay in sync with the theme source of truth:\\\\n\\\\n```css\\\\n@theme {\\\\n  --color-surface: oklch(18% 0.02 260);\\\\n  --color-border: oklch(28% 0.03 260);\\\\n  --font-sans: \\\\\\\"Inter\\\\\\\", system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif;\\\\n}\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nUse the generated classes (`bg-surface`, `border-border`, `font-sans`) instead of hardcoding values in components.\\\\n\\\\n- Centralize color, spacing, and typography via CSS variables when feasible.\\\\n- Prefer utilities referencing tokens; avoid ad-hoc hardcoded values.\\\\n- Document tokens and usage for contributors.\\\\n- Use mobile-first styles; apply breakpoints progressively.\\\\n- Prefer container queries where available; avoid fragile CSS overrides.\\\\n- Test across common device sizes and high-contrast modes.\\\\n\\\\n### Concrete Checks\\\\n- Use Tailwind v4 import syntax (no `@tailwind base/components/utilities`).\\\\n- Apply `font-sans` to text elements by default.\\\\n- Prefer utility classes; minimize custom CSS.\\\\n- Support light and dark modes.\\\\n\\\\n## Vitest Validation Context\\\\n\\\\n### Guidelines\\\\n### TDD workflow (Vitest)\\\\n\\\\n- Follow core TDD (see constitution): tests-first, minimal green, then refactor.\\\\n- Keep the loop tight: run the smallest scope that proves correctness, then expand.\\\\n\\\\n#### Micro-template\\\\n\\\\n```typescript\\\\nimport { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest'\\\\n\\\\ndescribe('feature', () => {\\\\n  it('RED: fails before implementation exists', () => {\\\\n    // Arrange\\\\n    // Act\\\\n    // Assert\\\\n    expect(actual).toEqual(expected)\\\\n  })\\\\n})\\\\n```\\\\n### Test quality (Vitest)\\\\n\\\\n- Use descriptive `describe`/`it` names that state **behavior**.\\\\n- Prefer outcome assertions over internal call assertions.\\\\n- Prefer user-facing assertions for UI; avoid brittle snapshots unless they add real value.\\\\n- Ensure proper setup/teardown; avoid shared mutable state.\\\\n\\\\n#### GOOD: behavior-focused, outcome assertions\\\\n\\\\n```typescript\\\\nimport { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest'\\\\n\\\\ndescribe('createItem', () => {\\\\n  it('rejects empty name with a typed error', () => {\\\\n    expect(() => createItem({ name: '' })).toThrow(/name/i)\\\\n  })\\\\n})\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n#### BAD: implementation-detail assertions as “proof”\\\\n\\\\n```typescript\\\\nimport { it, expect } from 'vitest'\\\\n\\\\nit('creates item', async () => {\\\\n  await createItem({ name: 'x' })\\\\n\\\\n  // ❌ proves only that an internal method was called, not that behavior is correct\\\\n  expect(internalDbClient.insert).toHaveBeenCalled()\\\\n})\\\\n```\\\\n### API testing (Vitest)\\\\n\\\\n- **Test the boundary**: Prefer exercising the real API boundary (real request/response) over calling internal helpers directly.\\\\n- **Assert contracts**: Status codes + response envelope shape + key fields.\\\\n- **Deterministic data**: Use per-test unique IDs / namespaces or transaction rollback (whatever your stack supports) to avoid cross-test collisions.\\\\n- **No internal mocking**: Do not mock internal auth/data/business modules as “proof”. If a boundary double is unavoidable, limit it to **external services you do not control**.\\\\n\\\\n#### Minimal illustrative pattern (pseudocode)\\\\n\\\\n```pseudocode\\\\ntest(\\\\\\\"returns 400 on invalid input\\\\\\\"):\\\\n  client = create_real_test_client()\\\\n\\\\n  res = client.post(\\\\\\\"/api/v1/items\\\\\\\", json={ name: \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\" })\\\\n\\\\n  assert res.status == 400\\\\n  assert res.json.error == \\\\\\\"Validation failed\\\\\\\"\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n#### Anti-patterns\\\\n\\\\n- Using `sleep()`/timeouts to “wait for consistency”\\\\n- Reusing static IDs across tests (not parallel-safe)\\\\n- Asserting internal call counts instead of observable outcomes\\\\n### Component testing (Vitest + Testing Library)\\\\n\\\\n- Interact like users: drive events and assert DOM updates.\\\\n- Prefer queries by role/label/text; avoid test IDs unless necessary.\\\\n- Keep tests isolated; render fresh components per test.\\\\n\\\\n#### Minimal illustrative pattern\\\\n\\\\n```typescript\\\\nimport { it, expect } from 'vitest'\\\\nimport { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react'\\\\nimport userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event'\\\\n\\\\nit('submits form', async () => {\\\\n  const user = userEvent.setup()\\\\n  render(<MyForm />)\\\\n\\\\n  await user.type(screen.getByLabelText(/email/i), 'a@b.com')\\\\n  await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: /submit/i }))\\\\n\\\\n  expect(await screen.findByText(/success/i)).toBeInTheDocument()\\\\n})\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n### Concrete Checks\\\\n- Avoid `.skip()`/`.only()` in committed code.\\\\n- Enforce the core NO MOCKS policy: mock only system boundaries (third-party APIs), never internal modules.\\\\n- Keep tests fast and deterministic with clear naming.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Output Format\\\\n\\\\n```markdown\\\\n# Global Validation Report\\\\n\\\\n**Task**: [Task ID]\\\\n**Status**: ✅ APPROVED | ⚠️ APPROVED WITH WARNINGS | ❌ REJECTED\\\\n**Timestamp**: [ISO 8601]\\\\n\\\\n## Summary\\\\n[2-3 sentences]\\\\n\\\\n## Validation Results\\\\n### 1-10.
